definitions.explanation: A Buddhist sacred text, originally referring to the recorded teachings of the Buddha. One of the three divisions of the Buddhist canon ({三蔵|さんぞう}). Also used more broadly for the chanting of such texts.

examples.japanese: {僧侶|そうりょ}が{経|きょう}を{唱|とな}えた。
{般若心経|はんにゃしんぎょう}は{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{親|した}しまれている{経|きょう}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: The Heart Sutra is one of the most familiar sutras in Japan.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{仏壇|ぶつだん}の{前|まえ}で{経|きょう}を{読|よ}むのを{日課|にっか}にしている。
examples.english: My grandmother makes it a daily habit to read sutras in front of the Buddhist altar every morning.

notes:
The standalone reading {経|きょう} refers specifically to Buddhist scriptures. The same kanji has many other readings and meanings ({経|けい} as in {経済|けいざい} 'economy,' {経験|けいけん} 'experience').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経|きょう}を{唱|とな}える: to chant a sutra
- {経|きょう}を{読|よ}む: to read/recite a sutra
- {経|きょう}を{上|あ}げる: to chant a sutra (for the deceased)
- お{経|きょう}: sutra (polite form, very common)

IMPORTANT SUTRAS:
- {般若心経|はんにゃしんぎょう}: Heart Sutra — the most commonly chanted
- {法華経|ほけきょう}: Lotus Sutra — central to Nichiren Buddhism
- {阿弥陀経|あみだきょう}: Amitabha Sutra — central to Pure Land Buddhism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{経|きょう}: sutra (polite) — the most common everyday form; used in speech about funerals and daily devotion
- {経典|きょうてん}: scripture; canonical text — the formal/academic term for sacred texts
- {仏典|ぶってん}: Buddhist texts — broader category including commentaries and treatises
